components.name: BackButton
components.description: A button going back in a router's history, disabled at its start, its right click listing the pages before: a macOS toolbar item, a 36-point platter with a hairline around SF Symbols' chevron, shared with ForwardButton in a Toolbar, Windows 11's NavigationView back button with its arrow, or GNOME's flat image button with go-previous-symbolic, as in a header bar.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.description: A path whose items but the last are links: macOS's NSPathControl in secondaryLabelColor with chevrons, Windows 11's BreadcrumbBar, or the path bar of GNOME's Files, bold buttons separated by slashes in a trough.

components.name: ForwardButton
components.description: A button going forward in a router's history, drawn as BackButton is on each platform, its glyph pointing the other way.

components.name: Sidebar
components.description: A sidebar of sections and items, which the arrows and typing choose among: macOS's source list, its selection in the accent color while it has the focus and gray otherwise, Windows 11's NavigationView pane, or GNOME's AdwSidebar.

components.name: SidebarItem
components.description: An item of a Sidebar with an optional icon: a 32-point source list row on macOS, its label semibold when chosen, a NavigationViewItem with its accent pill on Windows 11, a 42-pixel AdwSidebar row on GNOME.

components.name: SidebarSection
components.description: A section of a Sidebar that its title shows and hides, headed as the platform heads one: AppKit's group row, Windows 11's NavigationViewItemHeader, or AdwSidebar's bold heading on GNOME.

components.name: Toolbar
components.description: A row of controls along the top of a window, which the arrows move among and which puts those that do not fit in a menu, its buttons, toggles and menu buttons drawn as the platform's toolbar items: 52 points high with 36-point capsules 8 apart as a macOS window's toolbar, adjacent image items sharing a platter, Windows 11's CommandBar with AppBarButtons, or GNOME's .toolbar with flat image buttons.
